From 52d6c8c6ca125872459054daa70f2f1c698c8e75 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2015 17:03:41 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] net: pktgen: disable xmit_clone on virtual devices

Trying to use burst capability (aka xmit_more) on a virtual device
like bonding is not supported.

For example, skb might be queued multiple times on a qdisc, with
various list corruptions.

Fixes: 38b2cf2982dc ("net: pktgen: packet bursting via skb->xmit_more")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@plumgrid.com>
Acked-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@plumgrid.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/core/pktgen.c b/net/core/pktgen.c
index b4899f5b7388..508155b283dd 100644
--- a/net/core/pktgen.c
+++ b/net/core/pktgen.c
@@ -1134,6 +1134,9 @@ static ssize_t pktgen_if_write(struct file *file,
 			return len;
 
 		i += len;
+		if ((value > 1) &&
+		    (!(pkt_dev->odev->priv_flags & IFF_TX_SKB_SHARING)))
+			return -ENOTSUPP;
 		pkt_dev->burst = value < 1 ? 1 : value;
 		sprintf(pg_result, "OK: burst=%d", pkt_dev->burst);
 		return count;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/core/pktgen.c`**
- A new conditional check was added in the `pktgen_if_write` function. This check verifies if the `value` is greater than 1 and if the `priv_flags` of the underlying device (`pkt_dev->odev->priv_flags`) do not include `IFF_TX_SKB_SHARING`. If both conditions are met, the function returns `-ENOTSUPP`, indicating that the burst capability is not supported on virtual devices.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a bug related to the use of burst capability (xmit_more) on virtual devices, specifically bonding. The added check prevents the potential corruption of the skb queueing process by ensuring that burst transmission is only allowed on devices that support it. This change is a direct response to the issues identified in the previous commit (38b2cf2982dc) that introduced packet bursting via `skb->xmit_more`, thereby enhancing the stability and reliability of packet generation on virtual devices.
